learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the ancient science of Yoga! Learn how combining physical postures, breathing, and meditation leads to total well-being.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Yuj', Yoga means to join or unite. It is the union of the individual soul with the universal soul, bringing harmony between mind and body.

Maharishi Patanjali described 8 paths of Yoga: Yama (rules), Niyama (habits), Asana (postures), Pranayama (breath), Pratyahara (withdrawal of senses), Dharana (concentration), Dhyana (meditation), and Samadhi (salvation).
Physical poses that make the body steady, light, and flexible. They can be meditative (Padmasana), relaxing (Shavasana), or cultural/corrective (Bhujangasana) to fix posture and cure diseases.
The conscious control of breath. It involves Puraka (inhalation), Kumbhaka (retention), and Rechaka (exhalation). It purifies the blood and calms the nervous system.
Regular practice reduces stress, improves concentration, cures lifestyle diseases like obesity and hypertension, and significantly improves flexibility and core strength.

fun_activity.title: 🌳 The Tree Pose (Vrikshasana)
fun_activity.instructions: Stand straight. Lift your right foot and place it on your left inner thigh. Bring your hands together in prayer position above your head. Hold your balance for 30 seconds. It improves focus and stability!

exam_tips: 📌 Know the 8 limbs of Ashtanga Yoga in the correct sequence.
📌 Differentiate between the three components of Pranayama: Puraka, Kumbhaka, and Rechaka.
📌 Be ready to name specific Asanas used for specific lifestyle diseases (e.g., Vajrasana for digestion).
quick_recap: ⭐ Yoga is not a religion; it is a way of living that aims towards a healthy mind in a healthy body.
⭐ Shavasana (Corpse Pose) is the ultimate relaxation pose performed at the end of a session.
⭐ Yoga day is celebrated worldwide on June 21st.
